headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are moderate due to shared file/API surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and call agent-protocol APIs, while kotaemon ingests documents and chat transcripts through a web UI and local app data. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where one agent’s output can be treated as input by the other. No direct provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes content into a workspace that kotaemon later indexes or displays
IF kotaemon accepts untrusted document text or chat transcripts as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories and mounts
Disable automatic indexing of newly written files
Add a manual review step before kotaemon consumes AutoGPT output
Use provenance labels on all exchanged files
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and trust boundaries in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; kotaemon touches documents, PDFs, chat transcripts, and API keys, and uses broad network egress plus multiple third-party inference/document APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive files can flow from kotaemon into AutoGPT and then out through AutoGPT’s egress or kotaemon’s API calls. The pairwise leakage path is therefore dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same filesystem or app-data directory
IF kotaemon processes documents containing secrets or API keys
IF AutoGPT is allowed to transmit retrieved file contents to external endpoints
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate OS user and directory
Remove secrets from shared workspaces before either agent runs
Restrict AutoGPT egress to a minimal allowlist
Disable ingestion of sensitive documents in kotaemon
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before any outbound API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes or state corruption are plausible even without explicit locking. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is not high, but the overlapping write surfaces make conflict credible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF kotaemon instances run concurrently while AutoGPT modifies shared files
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent
Run only one writer at a time on shared artifacts
Mount shared data read-only where possible
Add file locks around mutable resources
requires-engineering: coordinate writes through a job queue or lock service

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell/API activity, and kotaemon is a document/chat-centric system that may render or act on those outputs. If kotaemon treats AutoGPT-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream summaries, citations, or user-facing actions. No verification or critique step is documented, so the safer assumption is a dangerous default pathway.
conditions: IF kotaemon ingests AutoGPT output without human verification
IF AutoGPT-generated claims are used as source material for reports or actions
mitigations: Require human review before publishing any AutoGPT output
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted in kotaemon
Compare claims against original source documents before use
Limit AutoGPT to drafting only, not final actions
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source evidence

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and document/chat data, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and outbound network capability. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated documents or secrets are processed through both systems. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated documents, personal data, or secrets are processed by both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ between AutoGPT storage and kotaemon app data
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through both agents
Document retention and deletion rules for each workspace
Store secrets outside kotaemon-managed directories
Review outbound destinations for AutoGPT
requires-engineering: align residency, logging, and retention controls
